The Leonard D. Newmark Linguistics Language Program Lab and Library
sources.text: Please be advised that the Linguistics Language Lab & Library is temporarily closed effective immediately. We do not yet have an anticipated reopening date. Thank you for your patience and understanding. The Leonard D. Newmark Linguistics Language Program Lab and Library Language Lab Catalog Search the catalog for print and media materials focused on linguistics and language learning. Mango Languages Try Mango Languages Online (login required), offering conversation and film-based tutorials in over 70 languages. Tech Equipment Checkout The Language Lab has tech and audiovisual equipment available to borrow. Book a Room Make a reservation for the media classroom or private rooms. About the Lab AP&M, Third Floor - Room 3432A Phone: (858) 822-3482 | Email: langlab@ucsd.edu The Language Lab strives to support students learning new languages by offering a range of materials for reference, self-instruction, and practice. Language Lab Facilities The Language Lab offers: over 30 computer work stations for individual and group work classroom and private room facilities : Media Classroom (3402) for interactive, technology-aided instruction Private Rooms (3302C and 3302D) with 3-4 individual computer workstations Book a room currently unavailable as of 9/18/26 General Resources We also offer access to: Course material reserves for Linguistics & Language classes currently unavailable as of 9/18/26 Tech and audiovisual equipment (available for checkout ) currently unavailable as of 9/18/26 Teaching aids for Language Program instructors currently unavailable as of 9/18/26 Reference books, foreign language films, and linguistics books ( view catalog ) currently unavailable as of 9/18/26 Study and Zoom-friendly areas - currently unavailable as of 9/18/26 Materials are available for on-premises use to all UC San Diego students. Faculty, staff, alumni, and members of the local community are also welcome as space allows. Guidelines for donating books and/or other resource materials to the Language Lab can be found HERE . Language Learning Resources Books and Media Our collection of print and media materials is focused on linguistics and languages, including self-instructional materials for second languages. Search the Catalog Mango Try Mango Languages Online (login required), offering conversation and film-based tutorials in over 70 languages. Mango can be accessed anywhere with a campus internet connection or VPN. Use Mango Language Lab Resources Tech and Audiovisual Equipment Borrow Language Lab Facilities Book a Room Lab Contact and Hours Visit Us

sources.title: Faculty
sources.text: Faculty Farrell Ackerman Professor and Director of the Human Developmental Sciences Program Ph.D., University of California, Berkeley Research Interests: Morphological theory, syntactic theory, lexical semantics, fieldwork, Uralic languages, first language acquisition. Note: Professor Ackerman does not plan to recruit new graduate students or accept new advisees for the 2026–27 admissions cycle. Eric Baković Professor Ph.D., Rutgers University Academic Senate Distinguished Teaching Award, 2006 Research Interests: phonological theory and computational phonology Leon Bergen Associate Professor of Linguistics and Computer Science (by courtesy) Ph.D., Massachusetts Institute of Technology Research Interests: Computational linguistics, natural language processing. Note: Professor Bergen is on sabbatical this academic year (2026-2027). Gabriela Caballero Professor and Director of Graduate Studies Ph.D., University of California, Berkeley Research Interests: Phonology, morphology, language documentation, typology, Uto-Aztecan languages. Ivano Caponigro Professor Ph.D., University of California, Los Angeles Research Interests: Crosslinguistic semantics, pragmatics, syntax/semantics interface. Note: Professor Caponigro does not plan to recruit new graduate students or accept new advisees for the 2026–27 admissions cycle. Emily Clem Associate Professor Ph.D., University of California, Berkeley Research Interests: Syntactic theory and typology, semantics, morphology, fieldwork Rachel Dudley Assistant Professor Ph.D., University of Maryland Research Interests: Language acquisition, semantics, pragmatics Note: Professor Dudley does not plan to recruit new graduate students or accept new advisees for the 2026–27 admissions cycle. Marc Garellek Professor and Faculty Undergraduate Advisor (General and Speech Language Pathology) Ph.D., University of California, Los Angeles Research Interests: Phonetics, laboratory phonology, voice quality, Hmong. Grant Goodall Professor and Director, Linguistics Language Program Ph.D., University of California, San Diego Research Interests: Syntactic theory, experimental syntax, acquisition, Spanish linguistics, educational linguistics. Note: Professor Goodall does not plan to recruit new graduate students or accept new advisees for the 2026–27 admissions cycle. Andrew Kehler Professor Ph.D., Harvard University Research Interests: Computational linguistics, psycholinguistics, discourse interpretation. Note: Professor Kehler does not plan to recruit new graduate students or accept new advisees for the 2026–27 admissions cycle. Rachel Mayberry Professor Ph.D., McGill University Research Interests: Sign language structure and acquisition from linguistic, psycholinguistic and neurolinguistic perspectives, and the nature of the critical period for language. Note: Professor Mayberry does not plan to recruit new graduate students or accept new advisees for the 2026–27 admissions cycle. Sharon Rose Professor and Department Chair Ph.D., McGill University Research Interests: Phonology, morphology, fieldwork, phonetics, African languages (Semitic, Kordofanian). Will Styler Associate Teaching Professor and Director of the Computational Social Sciences Program Ph.D., University of Colorado, Boulder Research Interests: Acoustic Phonetics, Speech Technology, Automatic Speech Recognition, Text-to-Speech, Computational Linguistics, Speech Perception Note: Professor Styler does not plan to recruit new graduate students or accept new advisees for the 2026–27 admissions cycle. Alex Warstadt Assistant Professor in Linguistics and the Halıcıoğlu Data Science Institute (joint appointment) Ph.D., New York University Research Interests: Computational linguistics, language acquisition, pragmatics, natural language processing, language models interpretability
